frequently_asked_questions.question: How often does my Porsche need service?
frequently_asked_questions.answer: Most Porsche vehicles with internal combustion engines require service every 10,000 miles or 12 months, whichever comes first. The Taycan and other electric models have longer intervals of 20,000 miles or 24 months. Your vehicle's onboard maintenance reminder will also alert you when service is due.

frequently_asked_questions.question: How do I schedule a service appointment?
frequently_asked_questions.answer: You can schedule a service appointment by calling your preferred Porsche dealer directly, using the Porsche Connect app on your smartphone, or visiting your dealer's website. We recommend booking at least one to two weeks in advance, especially for major services.

frequently_asked_questions.question: What is included in a Porsche service?
frequently_asked_questions.answer: A standard Porsche service includes an engine oil and filter change for combustion models, a multi-point inspection covering brakes, tires, fluids, and electronics, plus a cabin air filter check. Major services add items like spark plugs, air filters, brake fluid flush, and transmission fluid checks.

frequently_asked_questions.question: Can I take my Porsche to an independent mechanic?
frequently_asked_questions.answer: While you are free to have your Porsche serviced anywhere, we strongly recommend using an authorized Porsche dealer. Our factory-trained technicians use Porsche-specific diagnostic equipment and genuine parts. Service at unauthorized facilities may affect your warranty coverage.

frequently_asked_questions.question: Does Porsche offer pickup and delivery for service?
frequently_asked_questions.answer: Many Porsche dealers offer complimentary pickup and delivery service for scheduled maintenance. Some dealers also offer mobile service for certain minor repairs. Check with your local dealer for availability in your area.

frequently_asked_questions.question: How long does a typical service take?
frequently_asked_questions.answer: A minor service typically takes two to four hours. A major service may take a full day. Your service advisor will provide a time estimate when you schedule. Many dealers offer loaner vehicles or a comfortable waiting area with amenities.

frequently_asked_questions.question: What is Porsche Connect?
frequently_asked_questions.answer: Porsche Connect is a suite of digital services that enhance your driving experience. It includes remote vehicle status monitoring, navigation with real-time traffic, Apple CarPlay integration, remote climate control, and vehicle tracking. A complimentary subscription is included for the first three years with new vehicles.

frequently_asked_questions.question: How do I check my warranty status?
frequently_asked_questions.answer: You can check your warranty status by contacting your Porsche dealer with your VIN number, logging into your My Porsche account online, or calling Porsche Customer Care at 1-800-PORSCHE. Your service advisor can also review your warranty coverage during any dealer visit.

frequently_asked_questions.question: What does Porsche Roadside Assistance cover?
frequently_asked_questions.answer: Porsche Roadside Assistance provides 24/7 support including towing to the nearest Porsche dealer, flat tire assistance, jump start service, lockout help, and emergency fuel delivery. It also includes trip interruption benefits covering hotel, meals, and rental car costs if you're stranded away from home. It's included for four years with new vehicles.

frequently_asked_questions.question: Can I transfer my warranty to a new owner?
frequently_asked_questions.answer: Yes, both the new vehicle warranty and the Porsche Approved CPO warranty are fully transferable to subsequent owners at no additional cost. The warranty terms and coverage remain the same for the remainder of the original warranty period.

frequently_asked_questions.question: What are N-rated tires?
frequently_asked_questions.answer: N-rated tires are specifically developed and tested by Porsche in collaboration with tire manufacturers. They are marked with N0, N1, N2, or similar designations on the sidewall. While not mandatory, Porsche recommends N-rated tires for optimal performance, handling, and safety characteristics matched to your specific model.

frequently_asked_questions.question: How do I know if my vehicle has an open recall?
frequently_asked_questions.answer: You can check for open recalls by providing your VIN to your Porsche dealer, visiting the NHTSA website at nhtsa.gov/recalls, or checking your My Porsche account. Porsche also sends direct mail notifications to registered owners when a recall is issued for their vehicle.

frequently_asked_questions.question: What is Porsche Approved Certified Pre-Owned?
frequently_asked_questions.answer: Porsche Approved CPO vehicles undergo a rigorous 111-point inspection, come with a two-year unlimited mileage warranty, include 24/7 Roadside Assistance, and are backed by a complete vehicle history review. Only vehicles under 15 years old purchased from authorized dealers qualify for the program.

frequently_asked_questions.question: Does Porsche offer loaner vehicles during service?
frequently_asked_questions.answer: Most authorized Porsche dealers offer complimentary loaner vehicles for scheduled maintenance and warranty repairs. Availability may vary, so we recommend requesting a loaner when you book your service appointment. Some dealers offer Porsche loaner vehicles so you can continue enjoying the Porsche driving experience.

frequently_asked_questions.question: How do I order genuine Porsche parts?
frequently_asked_questions.answer: Genuine Porsche parts can be ordered through your local authorized dealer, the Porsche Tequipment online shop, or by calling the dealer's parts department directly. For classic Porsche models, Porsche Classic maintains a catalog of over 60,000 parts. Your dealer can also special-order any part not currently in stock.

frequently_asked_questions.question: What is the Porsche Extended Warranty?
frequently_asked_questions.answer: The Porsche Extended Warranty offers continued coverage beyond the standard four-year, 50,000-mile factory warranty. Plans are available in Platinum and Gold tiers, with coverage up to 10 years or 150,000 miles. It must be purchased before your factory warranty expires and can be used at any authorized Porsche dealer nationwide.

frequently_asked_questions.question: How do I maintain my Porsche battery when not driving?
frequently_asked_questions.answer: If your Porsche will be parked for an extended period, we recommend using a Porsche-approved battery maintainer or trickle charger. For the Taycan and hybrid models, keep the high-voltage battery charged between 20% and 80%. Avoid letting any Porsche sit for more than four weeks without starting or maintaining the battery.

frequently_asked_questions.question: What payment methods are accepted for service?
frequently_asked_questions.answer: Authorized Porsche dealers typically accept all major credit cards, debit cards, personal checks, and financing options for larger repairs. Some dealers also offer Porsche Financial Services for service payment plans. Check with your specific dealer for available payment methods.

frequently_asked_questions.question: Can I get a service cost estimate before bringing my car in?
frequently_asked_questions.answer: Yes, your service advisor can provide a detailed estimate before any work is performed. For scheduled maintenance, most dealers publish standard pricing. For diagnostic or repair work, an initial diagnostic fee may apply, and you will receive a full estimate for approval before any additional work begins.

frequently_asked_questions.question: What should I do if my Porsche warning light comes on?
frequently_asked_questions.answer: If a warning light appears, consult your owner's manual for the specific indicator meaning. Red warning lights require immediate attention — pull over safely and contact Porsche Roadside Assistance. Yellow warning lights indicate a condition that should be checked soon. In either case, schedule a diagnostic appointment with your Porsche dealer as soon as possible.
